focus: Lead with the literal reading ('those who resemble each other gather together'); the ressemble/assemble rhyme is the built-in hook – drop the teacherly 'aids memorization' framing.
The insight is 'demeure entière' = literally 'remains whole' – no part of the question has been answered; keep the formal-register note in one clause.
'Habit' is a false friend – French habit = garment (here the monk's robe), not a routine; quote 'l'habit'/'le moine' and keep the literal image.
'Nous nous garderons de' is literally 'we will guard ourselves from' – the reflexive guard-yourself image explains why French refrains reflexively; quote the card.
Explain the construction standalone (its sibling 'force est de' sat on the wrong card): 'force m'est de' = roughly 'necessity is upon me to' – the m' marks who is compelled.
Cut the re-translation half; the one rule is the conditional 'serait' as academic hedging – French softens claims with the conditional.
'Nous nous attacherons à' = literally 'we will attach ourselves to' demonstrating – the vivid literal image explains the phrasing; cut the bare gloss shape.
The real trap is the missing preposition: pallier takes a direct object ('pallier les insuffisances'), never 'pallier à' – unlike remédier à; even natives get this wrong.
Anchor in the card by quoting 'ont toujours tort' (avoir tort = literally 'to have wrong') and keep the meaning – the absent can't defend themselves, so they get the blame.
The reusable insight is the X-à-X doubling pattern: petit à petit, peu à peu, côte à côte – drop the gloss that duplicates the translation and the generic 'common in proverbs' claim.
The hook is the literal reading: 'far from the eyes, far from the heart' – French says heart (cœur) where English says mind; drop the verbless-parallelism structure talk.
Keep the literal 'to a good cat, a good rat' + matched-opponents meaning, but quote the French ('À bon chat, bon rat') and lose the bare 'Proverb. Literal:' shape.
Quote 'Errare humanum est'; the useful fact is that formal French drops Latin tags whole – keep the famous continuation ('perseverare diabolicum') as the one extra beat, nothing else.
